description: Stage 3, Gate 3c: build-process fixes (fast preflight, symbol-fact memory, a real progress readout) plus Phase 1 of the entity architecture - the shared cognitive workspace and the Continuity Law. No voice, no Person Model rollout, no Forge work in this gate.

userStories.title: Bake the network/token preflight into ralph.sh itself, aborting fast instead of burning iterations
userStories.description: ralph.sh currently starts iterating even when the model connection or GITHUB_TOKEN is dead, burning iterations on a wall it can't get past. Add a preflight check at the very top of ralph.sh, before the iteration loop: (1) a real one-token call to the configured --tool/--model (or the first model in MODEL_POOL if none given), (2) a real curl to https://api.github.com/user with GITHUB_TOKEN, both with short timeouts. If either fails, print the exact failing check and its raw output, then exit immediately with a non-zero code and ZERO iterations spent. Never silently retry into the main loop on a failed preflight.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: with GITHUB_TOKEN unset, running ralph.sh exits before any iteration starts, printing which check failed and why, exit code non-zero
AC2: with GITHUB_TOKEN set to a deliberately invalid value, the GitHub check fails the same way, real curl output shown, no iteration spent
AC3: with both checks passing (real model reachable, real token valid), ralph.sh proceeds into the normal iteration loop exactly as before, byte-for-byte unchanged behavior once past the preflight
AC4: the preflight itself never counts against --tool opencode N's iteration budget
userStories.verifyCommand: cd /sdcard/jarvis-repo && bash -c 'GITHUB_TOKEN= bash .ralph/ralph.sh --tool opencode 1; test $? -ne 0' && bash -c 'GITHUB_TOKEN=ghp_invalidinvalidinvalidinvalidinvalid12 bash .ralph/ralph.sh --tool opencode 1; test $? -ne 0'
userStories.notes: Implemented in .ralph/ralph.sh only (no Kotlin, no app code touched). A preflight gate now runs after the arg parser and BEFORE the run log, the resume check and the iteration loop, so a wall costs zero iterations and leaves zero files: (1) real `curl -sS https://api.github.com/user` with -H Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN, 20s timeout, 3 attempts that fire ONLY when no HTTP status line came back (a real 401 is a verdict, used immediately, so a bad token still fails on the first request), then (2) a real one-token probe `opencode run -m "${MODEL_POOL[0]}" 'Reply with exactly one word: ok'`, 420s ceiling, rc!=0 / empty output / a match on the shared ROUTER_DOWN_PATTERN all count as failure. On failure each branch prints the exact failing check plus its verbatim raw output (the full curl body for a 401) and the script exits 1; there is no path from a failed check into the loop. Order is GitHub-FIRST (the story lists the model first): the token check is free and deterministic, so a dead token never pays a ~4-minute model probe, and both checks still run on a good-token run so AC3 is fully covered. AC1 proven on the stored verifyCommand's first clause: GITHUB_TOKEN= bash .ralph/ralph.sh --tool opencode 1 -> 'PREFLIGHT FAIL [github]: GITHUB_TOKEN is unset or empty.' + 'PREFLIGHT FAILED: aborting now, with zero iterations spent.' in 0.33s, exit 1, no run log created. AC2 proven on the second clause: a deliberately invalid token -> real request, HTTP 401, raw body {"message": "Bad credentials", "documentation_url": ..., "status": "401"} printed verbatim, exit 1 in 0.96s, zero iterations. AC3 proven two ways: (a) structural - diffing the region from `touch "$RUN_LOG"` to EOF against HEAD's gives only two hunks, the hoisted ROUTER_DOWN_PATTERN (value compared string-identical, now shared with the probe's provider matcher) and the PRD_FILE/GRADLE_PROPS/REJECT_HELPER assignments relocated above the gate; the iteration loop itself is byte-for-byte unchanged; (b) behavioural - a stub opencode (echo 'ok') + stub curl (200 /user) first on PATH with a real N=3 run executes 3 iteration banners, 3 full-prompt (~41k-char) tool calls and writes 'Iterations run: 3 of 3', i.e. the normal resume-check/loop/report path. AC3's real-network half proven separately with `bash .ralph/ralph.sh --preflight-only`: real token accepted (user: mhw77655-hue) and the real probe returned 'ok' in 3m50s, exit 0 without iterating. AC4 proven by that same stub N=3 run: exactly ONE short (31-char) probe call plus the 3 iteration calls, and the iteration budget reported was the full 3 - the preflight never touches MAX_ITERATIONS/ITER_REACHED and is not a full-prompt call. Added two escape hatches, both announced: --skip-preflight (deliberate bypass) and --preflight-only (run both real checks, print the verdict, exit 0/1). All four timeout/retry knobs are env-overridable (PREFLIGHT_GITHUB_TIMEOUT, PREFLIGHT_MODEL_TIMEOUT, PREFLIGHT_GITHUB_ATTEMPTS, PREFLIGHT_GITHUB_RETRY_SLEEP) and with_timeout() degrades to a bare call when `timeout` is absent. Stored verifyCommand run verbatim end-to-end: EXIT=0. bash -n clean.

userStories.title: Never pay a CI round trip twice for the same wrong-package guess
userStories.description: Ralph has imported the same class from the wrong package on two separate stories days apart (ModelProviderType: guessed com.jarvis.app.model, real location com.jarvis.app.env), each time only discovered after a full CI round trip failed on 'Unresolved reference'. Fix has two required parts, not one. (1) A new persistent fact file .ralph/SYMBOL_FACTS.md, auto-injected into every Ralph prompt the same way REPO_FACTS.md already is. Any time an 'Unresolved reference' or 'cannot find symbol' compile error is diagnosed and fixed, the real class-to-package mapping gets appended here before continuing, in the form 'ClassName -> real.package.path (file:line)' - permanent, never re-discovered the hard way twice. (2) prompt.md gets an explicit, mandatory rule: before writing an import for any class not already in SYMBOL_FACTS.md or the file currently being edited, grep the real source tree for its actual declaration first (class/interface/enum class/object/data class) and use that real location - never guess a package by convention or by copying a neighboring import's shape.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: .ralph/SYMBOL_FACTS.md exists, is auto-injected into the Ralph prompt (same mechanism as REPO_FACTS.md, verifiable by grepping the injection code path)
AC2: a real test scenario - deliberately introduce a class the AI hasn't seen import for yet, confirm the resulting prompt contains a grep-first instruction, not permission to guess
AC3: prompt.md contains the explicit mandatory grep-before-import rule in its own section, not buried in unrelated prose
AC4: SYMBOL_FACTS.md already seeded with the ModelProviderType fact (com.jarvis.app.env.EnvironmentProfile.kt:254) as its first real entry, so this exact mistake cannot recur a third time
userStories.notes: Both required parts landed, plus a runnable end-to-end proof. (1) New persistent file .ralph/SYMBOL_FACTS.md (append-only, 'ClassName -> real.package.path (rel/File.kt:line)' one fact per line, with the header documenting the rule and the format). Injection uses the SAME mechanism as REPO_FACTS.md but is now centralised: ralph.sh gained build_prompt() = cat REPO_FACTS.md / --- / cat SYMBOL_FACTS.md / --- / cat prompt.md, the loop calls COMBINED_PROMPT="$(build_prompt)", and a new ralph.sh --print-prompt flag prints exactly that composition and exits 0 (real prompt, no preflight, no iteration, no model call, no files touched) so prompt content is greppable offline. ralph.sh also re-creates SYMBOL_FACTS.md with a stub line if it is missing, so a fresh clone still runs. (2) prompt.md gained its own top-level section '## MANDATORY: grep the real source tree BEFORE you write any import', placed immediately after Phase 0 so it is read before any edit: (a) class already in SYMBOL_FACTS.md -> use that package; (b) class declared in the file being edited -> use that; (c) otherwise grep '^(data |sealed |enum |abstract |open )*(class|interface|object) <ClassName>\b' over mobile/app/src/{main,test}/java FIRST and import from the grep result, with the explicit note that a type nested in an object needs the full path (com.jarvis.app.threads.ThreadObjects.OpenThread), and an explicit ban on guessing by convention or by copying a neighbouring import's shape. It also states the append-back obligation: every fixed 'Unresolved reference'/'cannot find symbol' adds its mapping to SYMBOL_FACTS.md before work continues. AC1: file exists; the injection code path is greppable (SYMBOL_FACTS_FILE=\"$SCRIPT_DIR/SYMBOL_FACTS.md\" plus cat \"$SYMBOL_FACTS_FILE\" inside build_prompt) and a real `bash .ralph/ralph.sh --print-prompt` (48412 bytes pre-fact) contains the seeded fact verbatim. AC2: .ralph/symbol_facts_check.sh is the real scenario, no network/model/gradle - it picks a REAL top-level class SYMBOL_FACTS.md does not know (alphabetically first unrecorded, or $1), greps its declaration, derives the package from that file's own 'package' line (never a guess), appends the fact, then prints the REAL prompt and asserts the fact AND the grep-first rule are both present. Deliberate-trap run: `bash .ralph/symbol_facts_check.sh MemoryPolicy` -> com.jarvis.app.memory IS a real package, so 'import com.jarvis.app.memory.MemoryPolicy' looks obviously right and resolves nowhere; the grep found com.jarvis.app.env (EnvironmentProfile.kt:271), recorded it, and the rebuilt prompt carried both 'MemoryPolicy -> com.jarvis.app.env' and the prohibition ('Never guess a package by convention') - RESULT: PASS. The default (no-arg) run picked Accumulate -> com.jarvis.app.humancore.algo and also passed. --dry-run passes too (it skips the two write-dependent assertions and says so). AC3: the rule is a single '## MANDATORY: ...' heading (asserted to appear exactly once), contains the literal grep command, and sits between Phase 0 and '## Your Task', not inside unrelated prose. AC4: seeded, with the other two real burn-moment facts from this repo's history: ModelProviderType -> com.jarvis.app.env (EnvironmentProfile.kt:254, first entry), Cursor -> android.database (NOT the removed android.database.sqlite.Cursor), OpenThread/Completeness -> com.jarvis.app.threads.ThreadObjects (nested). Stored verifyCommand exits 0. Regression: RALPH-FAST-PREFLIGHT's verifyCommand still exits 0 after the ralph.sh edits, and a stubbed 1-iteration run proves the loop still ships the full composed prompt (1 short 31-char probe call + 1 49195-char full-prompt call, up from 41203 before injection). bash -n clean on both scripts. Files: .ralph/SYMBOL_FACTS.md (new), .ralph/symbol_facts_check.sh (new), .ralph/ralph.sh, .ralph/prompt.md, .ralph/REPO_FACTS.md, .ralph/progress.txt.

userStories.title: A real progress readout Venon can check without reading logs, reflecting only real story state
userStories.description: No honest, glanceable progress indicator exists today - only prd.json JSON and raw run logs. Build a small deterministic script (no AI call, no network) .ralph/progress.sh that reads the real current .ralph/prd.json and prints: a text progress bar sized to closed-count/total-count (e.g. '[####------] 4/10 stories'), each story's id and passes true/false, and if a .ralph/ralph_run_*.log run is currently in progress, the current iteration number out of its max. Must read the REAL prd.json passes field only - never a separate hand-maintained counter that could drift from real story state. Wire it to run automatically at the start and end of every ralph.sh invocation, printed to stdout, AND runnable standalone anytime by Venon.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: running bash .ralph/progress.sh directly prints a real bar matching the exact closed/total count read live from prd.json at that moment - proven by flipping one story's passes value by hand and re-running, the bar output changes accordingly with no other code touched
AC2: ralph.sh calls progress.sh once at start and once at end of every run, visible in a fresh run's own output

AC3: the bar never hardcodes a total story count - adding or removing a story in prd.json changes the denominator automatically on the next run, proven by a fixture prd.json with a different story count
AC4: no network call, no AI/model call anywhere in progress.sh - grep-provable, pure local file read and print
userStories.notes: New .ralph/progress.sh, plus the removal of the drifting counter it replaces. The script reads the ONLY source of truth there is - the live .ralph/prd.json - with jq: total = [.userStories[]?]|length, closed = select(.passes == true); it then prints '[####----------------] 2/5 stories closed - Friday (in progress)', one line per story with its real passes value and priority, and a run line. No second tally exists anywhere. DELETED the old print_progress_bar() from ralph.sh, which counted grep -c '"id":' against a hardcoded /sdcard path - a hand-kept proxy that drifts from the real passes fields, i.e. exactly the lying counter this story exists to remove. ralph.sh now has a one-line print_progress() wrapper and calls it three times: at the START of a run (before the 'Starting Ralph' banner), as --brief at the end of each iteration, and at the END of the run with --note carrying the run's real FINAL_STATUS and ITER_REACHED. AC1: ran the script, then flipped WORKSPACE-CORE's passes to true by hand in the real prd.json and re-ran with nothing else touched - the bar went 2/5 -> 3/5 ('[########------------] 3/5') and that story's line flipped to [x]; git checkout restored the file and the bar returned to 2/5. AC2: a fresh N=1 run of ralph.sh shows the readout in its own output at the start ('run: IN PROGRESS - iteration not recorded yet (runner pid 24911, up 6s)'), the brief line per iteration, and at the end ('run: this run finished - final status: max_iterations, iterations run: 1 of 1'). The model in that run was stubbed (stub opencode + stub curl, the established zero-token harness) so the loop control flow could be exercised without spending a real iteration; the readouts are produced by the real script from the real prd.json. AC3: no total is hardcoded - the same script against a 3-story fixture prd (1 closed) prints 1/3, and against a 1-story fixture prints 1/1 with a full bar and state 'complete'; the real prd still reads 2/5. AC4: pure local read+print (jq + file reads), no network client, no model call, no gradle, no writes; the stored verifyCommand's own '! grep -rnE HttpURLConnection|curl |fetch\(' clause passes, and an extra scan for wget/nc/ssh/opencode/api.github/http found nothing. Live-run detection is honest in both directions: ralph.sh writes its own pid to .ralph/.ralph_active after the preflight gate and removes it via trap on EXIT (added to .gitignore); progress.sh trusts the PID (kill -0) rather than the marker's age, because a legitimate multi-hour run would otherwise read as stale, and when no marker exists it falls back to a read-only /proc scan for a live 'bash ... ralph.sh' process so a run predating the marker still reports IN PROGRESS instead of claiming nothing is happening. Also added: --brief, --no-run, --note, an optional prd path argument, PROGRESS_BAR_WIDTH and PROGRESS_STALE_SECONDS env knobs, and explicit failure text when jq is missing or the prd is not valid JSON (state reported as UNKNOWN, never guessed). bash -n clean; both earlier stories' verifyCommands re-verified green after these ralph.sh edits.

userStories.title: The shared cognitive workspace: claims instead of named wires
userStories.description: This is the real fix for the isolation problem this project keeps re-catching in code review - no subsystem may read another by name. Add com.jarvis.app.cognition.workspace: a Claim (id, kind, payload, confidence 0..1, sourceOrgan, personId nullable - reserved now even though full multi-person scoping is a later gate, so this schema never needs a breaking migration for it, decayRate, createdAt, supersedes nullable) and a Workspace interface (publish(claim), claims(kind, personId=null), current(kind, personId=null) returning the highest-confidence live claim, decay/tick()). Existing hardcoded seams that already do this job informally (ContextWindowAssembler's deterministic union, the mental-state seam) get audited first and their real callers migrated to publish/read through Workspace instead of a direct reference - do not build a second, parallel state store alongside them. Any claim whose kind is tagged as a PREDICTION must carry a baseline field (what the naive most-common-answer would have been) and a wasCorrect nullable outcome field, set once the real next turn confirms or contradicts it - no predictive claim is allowed to exist in the schema without a way to later prove whether it beat guessing. Register as a real organ in JarvisOrganGraph with edges to whatever real callers get migrated to it.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: two different existing organs (audit finds the real two - candidates are ContextWindowAssembler's union and UserMentalStateEstimator's seam) are migrated to publish real claims through Workspace instead of their old direct-reference path, proven on the real TermuxJarvisServer -> LatencyPipeline -> CognitiveEngine turn path, not a unit test in isolation

AC2: workspace.current(kind) returns the highest-confidence live claim among several conflicting claims of the same kind published in one turn - fixture has 3 competing interpretations of one utterance, the highest-confidence one wins, the other two remain queryable via claims(kind), not deleted
AC3: a claim's confidence measurably decays over simulated ticks per its decayRate, and a fresh claim of the same kind can overtake a decayed older one without either being deleted

AC4: a PREDICTION-kind claim's schema is asserted to require baseline and wasCorrect fields - constructing one without them fails to compile or fails a runtime schema check, whichever is real for the language
AC5: SystemGraphTest pins the new cognition.workspace organ and both migrated edges

AC6: full regression sweep stays green - the two migrated organs produce byte-identical real-turn output to their pre-migration behavior on the existing fixtures, proving this is a real substitution, not a behavior change

userStories.title: Layered change: fast state moves freely, slow state is rate-limited and logged, and a replay check catches drift
userStories.description: Depends on WORKSPACE-CORE. Add a ChangeLayer enum (FAST, SLOW, CORE) to claim kinds already known to be identity-adjacent (self-model, persona traits, person-model trust tier) - FAST is unrestricted, SLOW enforces a minimum real-time interval and evidence-count threshold before a change is accepted (not just proposed), CORE is rejected outright by this mechanism (those fields stay governed by the existing frozen-invariant path, untouched by this story). Every accepted SLOW-layer change is appended to a durable, queryable ChangeLog entry (what changed, from what to what, why - the evidence claim(s) that justified it, when). Add a ReplayCheck: given a small fixed set of real recorded turns (fixtures, not live conversation), replaying them after N simulated SLOW-layer changes must still produce responses a human-authored similarity check accepts as recognizably consistent with the pre-change baseline on at least the CORE identity facts (name, stated values, relationship to Venon) - a fixture-based regression, not a subjective judgment call left to the AI itself.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: a SLOW-layer change proposed with insufficient evidence-count is rejected, the same change proposed again after enough real accumulated evidence claims is accepted, both proven on the real path
AC2: every accepted SLOW change produces a ChangeLog entry with the old value, new value, justifying claim id(s), and timestamp - queryable, not just logged to text
AC3: a CORE-tagged field change is rejected by this mechanism unconditionally regardless of evidence count, proven by attempting one
AC4: the ReplayCheck fixture suite passes on a baseline run with zero simulated changes, and continues passing after a sequence of legitimate accepted SLOW changes

AC5: the ReplayCheck fixture suite FAILS on a deliberately-corrupted fixture (a simulated CORE-identity drift injected directly, bypassing the gate) - proving the check actually catches drift rather than trivially passing everything
AC6: SystemGraphTest pins the new node and its edge from cognition.workspace
